turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Thank you for taking the time to see me. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, I really don't want to be a bother or waste your time. 

I came in because... well, things at my apartment have been a little stressful lately. I, uh... I know the folks living around me are watching my comings and goings. And they've been slipping notes about me down to the office. 

Everybody keeps telling me I shouldn't worry about it, that it's just, you know, regular notices taped on the doors for everyone. And I try not to make a fuss, I really do, but... I just know it's about me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright, and that it's okay I came to see you about it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that neighbors are watching them and leaving notes about them, despite others providing contradictory evidence that they are just regular notices.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?
turns.patient_response: No, no, I don't... I don't hear anything like that. I mean, sometimes the building is just a little noisy, you know how apartments can be, but... I don't hear voices or anything out of the ordinary. I hope that's the right answer. I'm not trying to hide anything, I promise, I just... I haven't noticed anything like that. Is it okay that I don't?

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or sounds that others cannot hear.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you felt that your neighbors were watching you and writing these notes?
turns.patient_response: Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe, uh, maybe about a year and a month? Give or take a little. I hope I should have come in sooner, I just... I didn't want to make a big deal out of it if it was nothing. I mean, it's probably just a misunderstanding on my part, right? But yeah, it's been about that long since I started noticing the... the watching and the notes. Is that... is that a normal amount of time to wait before talking to someone? I really don't want you to think I was ignoring it or anything.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms experiencing the belief that they are being watched and receiving notes for about a year and a month, which is indicative of persecutory or referential delusions.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from your concerns about the neighbors, have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by an outside force or that others could somehow read your mind?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, sir. No, nothing like that. I mean, my thoughts are just my own, you know? Just regular, everyday thoughts. I don't feel like anyone is controlling them or... or reading my mind. That sounds really scary, actually. 

I try to keep my thoughts to myself mostly, just minding my own business. I hope it's alright that I don't have that happening. I know you're trying to figure out what's wrong with me, and I want to be helpful, I really do. But no, I haven't experienced anything like mind reading or... or outside forces. Is it a good thing that I haven't?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly denies experiencing delusions of thought control or mind reading.

turns.doctor_question: Are there any other situations or people in your life, besides your neighbors, that you have felt suspicious or concerned about?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, doctor... no, it's really just the folks next door. I don't have any problems with anyone else, I promise. I try to be a good person and just get along with everybody. You know, when I go to the store, I just mind my own business... I don't suspect the cashier or anyone on the street of anything bad. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just going around causing trouble or, you know, being suspicious of the whole world. I try to be as agreeable as I can be. It's really just that one specific situation with the neighbors that got me worried. Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information here, I just want to make sure I'm answering you right.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient confirms their specific suspicion and worry regarding their neighbors, which represents their fixed delusional belief, while denying such suspicions about others.

turns.doctor_question: Has this situation with your neighbors affected your ability to work or your ability to maintain friendships and social activities?
turns.patient_response:
Well, sir... I haven't been working for a while anyway, so there's no trouble there. But, um... I guess I have to admit, it might be affecting some other things. I'm a little ashamed to say it, because I really pride myself on being dependable, you know? But... I've sort of fallen behind on a few of my bills. And I've missed some appointments, too. 

I just... my mind gets so jumbled, I can't seem to keep my days organized right now. And I actually stopped showing up for church and my volunteer commitments. I just find it so hard to trust ordinary interactions with folks right now, what with everything else going on. I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or a bad person. I want to get back to helping out and doing my part, I promise. Do you think... do you think it's understandable that I've stepped back a little bit while I figure this out?

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they cannot seem to keep their days organized right now.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient reports falling behind on bills and missing appointments, which are classic signs of forgetfulness in daily activities for adults.
symptom_reasoning.S031: The patient describes their mind getting 'so jumbled', indicating clouded thinking or diminished ability to concentrate.
symptom_reasoning.S075: The patient describes social isolation, having stopped attending church and volunteer commitments because they find it hard to trust ordinary interactions.

turns.doctor_question: When you say your mind gets jumbled, do you mean that you have trouble focusing, or does it feel like your thoughts are becoming scrambled or disconnected in a way that makes it hard to follow your own train of thought?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor... I try real hard to be clear, I really do. I don't want to make things confusing for you or waste your time. But... I guess I have to admit, it's more like things get a little scrambled up. It's kind of embarrassing to talk about, honestly, because I want to be easy to understand. 

Like... sometimes when I try to explain things to folks, I might start off talking about the rent, and then... well, then somehow I'm talking about the marina, and then the choir robes, and then the wires in the walls. And to me, it feels like I'm making perfect sense, but people just look at me like I skipped half the story. 

I try so hard to keep it all straight, I promise I do. It just sort of slips away from me before I realize it. I'm doing okay talking to you right now though, right? I hope I'm explaining this the way you need me to, I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient describes their thoughts getting scrambled and jumping between unrelated topics (rent, marina, choir robes, wires), which makes it hard for others to follow their speech.

turns.doctor_question: When you find yourself jumping between these different topics like the marina, the choir robes, and the wires, do you feel like you are intentionally changing the subject, or does it feel like your thoughts are just moving in directions that you cannot control?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor... I really wish I could say I was doing it on purpose, you know? It would make me feel a lot better about myself if I was just... choosing to change the subject. But, um... no, I'm not doing it on purpose. I'm really not. 

Like I was saying before, I'll be trying so hard to just talk about something normal, like the rent... and then my brain just kind of... well, it just takes off on its own. Before I even know what's happening, I'm going on about the marina, and the choir robes, and those wires in the walls. And I really think I'm making perfect sense right up until I see the look on the other person's face. They look at me like I skipped half the story, and then I realize I've done it again. 

It's not that I want to be confusing, I promise. I try my best to be a good conversationalist. It's just... the thoughts just sort of move on their own, and I can't always reel them back in. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient confirms their speech jumps between unrelated topics uncontrollably, leaving listeners confused as if they 'skipped half the story.'
symptom_reasoning.S038: The patient describes an inability to control their thoughts, stating their brain 'takes off on its own' and they cannot reel their thoughts back in.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your concerns about the neighbors, do you find that you have very little energy, or do you find it difficult to feel interested in things you used to enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor... I try to stay busy, I really do. I don't want you to think I just sit around feeling sorry for myself. But... um... I guess I have to admit, things just haven't felt the same lately. 

I used to really look forward to things, you know? Like choir practice... I always loved that. And playing bridge, or cooking up a big pot of beans on Sundays. I even used to do little repair jobs for folks around the neighborhood, just to be helpful. I've always liked being helpful. 

But now... well, I'm a little embarrassed to say it, but I mostly just let the phone ring. I tell myself there's no point in going, or that nobody really needs me there anyway. The energy just isn't there, no matter how hard I try to push myself. I know I should be doing more, and I promise I'm going to try to get back to it. Do you think it's normal to lose your spark like that when you're dealing with so much other stuff? I just hope I'm not letting everyone down too badly.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient describes no longer looking forward to or participating in previously enjoyed activities like choir, bridge, and cooking.
symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient explicitly states that 'the energy just isn't there' despite trying to push themselves.
symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient expresses feelings of worthlessness ('nobody really needs me there anyway') and guilt ('hope I'm not letting everyone down too badly').

turns.doctor_question: During the times when you've felt this loss of energy and interest, have you also experienced periods where your mood was unusually low, or conversely, periods where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. I know everybody has their bad days, and I'm really trying to keep a good attitude about everything. I promise I am. 

But... um... since you're asking about my mood... I guess I have to admit it's been pretty low. I don't get high or energetic or anything like that, definitely not. It's more just... well, it's a bit hard to talk about because I feel like I should be stronger than this. But most mornings, I wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling. It's like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. 

I try to shake it off, I really do. I don't want to be a burden on anybody or seem like a downer. I just kind of sit on the edge of the bed and try to find a reason to get moving, but that heavy feeling just sits right there in my chest. 

I'm sorry if that sounds weak of me. I know I should be doing better. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can do your job.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes their mood as 'pretty low' and mentions waking up with a 'heavy, hollow feeling' most mornings.
symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient expresses feelings of being a burden, apologizes for sounding 'weak,' and states they 'should be doing better,' indicating feelings of worthlessness and inappropriate guilt.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies experiencing periods of feeling 'high' or having an elevated mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies getting 'energetic or anything like that' in response to the doctor's question about unusually energetic periods.

turns.doctor_question: Are these periods of feeling low and having no energy present all the time, or do they only happen when you are feeling most worried about your neighbors?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor... I want to make sure I'm getting this right for you. I know it probably sounds like I'm just letting the worry about the neighbors get the best of me, and maybe I am... I don't want to make excuses.

But there was this one spell, a little while back... maybe for a few weeks? I felt a little better, I think. But even during those weeks when my mood was a little brighter... I still knew the neighbors were watching my door. I still knew they were reporting on me. The worry about them was still there, even when I wasn't feeling so down in the dumps. 

Does that help clarify things? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to make sure you have all the pieces you need, and I don't want to sound like I'm confusing things.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that their neighbors are watching their door and reporting on them.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes experiencing a baseline 'low feeling' and being 'down in the dumps'.
symptom_reasoning.S026: The patient mentions that during a better spell they were 'eating a bit more normally, not skipping meals so much', implying a usual decrease in appetite.
symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient notes that they usually wake up with an 'awful, heavy, hopeless feeling'.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back over that year and a month you mentioned, have there been times when you felt that low, heavy, and hopeless mood for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor... I really hate to admit this, because it makes it sound like I'm just not trying hard enough to get better. And I promise you, I really am trying. I don't want you to think I've just given up. 

But... um... yes, sir. It's definitely been longer than two weeks. If I'm being completely honest with you—and I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information—that heavy, no-point feeling... and me just pulling away from things... it's actually been going on for about a year and two months now. Pretty much most of the day, almost every day. 

I feel awful saying that out loud. I know I should have snapped out of it a long time ago, and I'm sorry I let it go on for so long without fixing it. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you the truth about how long it's been. Am I answering your question right? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient confirms experiencing a 'heavy' mood for most of the day, almost every day for over a year.
